reviews.title: Works like a charm with Ryzen 1800x
reviews.comment: Running an AMD Ryzen set up and this works just great, able to overclock to 3200 ghz with no problem and entirely stable.  I wanted to have a low profile memory to make way for the Noctua NF-A15 CPU cooler (an easy match!).  The only caveat, and it's a big one, is that when I was attempting to post for the first time the computer refused to post with all four DIMM slots occupied.  A relative found an obscure blog and found out that you should attempt your first post with only one of the DIMM slots occupied (I forget which, so that's helpful).  He found this out at two a.m., with me utterly demoralized on the couch.  Once it posted and I was able to flash the BIOS, it was no problem inserting all four of the DIMM slots and then incrementally cranking the speed of the memory.
reviews.author: Wilbur

reviews.title: AMD Type RAM
reviews.comment:
These RAM sticks are literally too expensive for what they offer, but I had to buy them to match my other RAM sticks to match the serial codes.
NOTE: YOU DO NOT NEED TO MATCH SERIAL CODES WHEN BUYING RAM. I only did so cuz my inention was to buy 4x sticks when I built my PC but I couldn't afford a second pair.
These sticks also DO NOT support overclocking on AMD CPUs, but they are advertised like they do. These RAM Sticks only really work with the XMP/EXPO Profile on the BIOS/UEFI. The person who helped me pick out parts for my machine that had suggested these RAM Sticks.... well he tried overclocking the memory with this set and it just wouldn't do it. It would clear back to the original EXPO profile that existed on the BIOS at reboot.
